title: Salisbury Cathedral from the Bishop's Grounds

image.credit: Photograph via Wikimedia Commons (John Constable - Salisbury Cathedral from the Bishop's Grounds.jpg)

source.label: Wikipedia: “Salisbury, a city whose cathedral and surrounding landscape were to inspire some of his greatest paintings”
Constable: “made my escape in the evanescence of the chiaroscuro”
Museum record (Wikidata): oil paint on canvas

work.text: It was the most difficult subject in landscape I ever had on my easel. I have not flinched at the windows, buttresses, &c., but I have still kept to my grand organ colour, and have, as usual, made my escape in the evanescence of the chiaroscuro.

source.author: John Constable
source.title: Letter to John Fisher, 9 May 1823, in C. R. Leslie, Life and Letters of John Constable, R.A. (1896 ed.)

work.text: Constable visited Salisbury in 1811 and made a series of sketches of the cathedral, from the south-east, the south-west and from the east end.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Salisbury Cathedral from the Bishop's Grounds

moment.text: It is an extremely beautiful work, and one with which he took great pains — a view of the Cathedral from the Bishop's Grounds.

source.author: C. R. Leslie
source.title: Life and Letters of John Constable, R.A. (1896 ed.)

moment.text: His patron took exception to the dark cloud over the cathedral, and when he commissioned a smaller replica, requested "a more serene sky".

source.author: Wikipedia contributors

matters.text: Included in the paintings are figures of Dr. Fisher and his wife at the bottom left.
